question: On many-lights-v1, how much GPU time is analytic-light crossing (every ray tests every light) versus the light-count-independent remainder that contains NEE/MIS light selection?
procedure: lotus-headless --benchmark, many-lights-v1, MIS, 64 bounces, 8 warmup + 64 measured frames, 128 and 512 pixels, Reference and Wavefront, 3 fresh processes per configuration in run-major round-robin order; validation and synchronization validation active; clocks unlocked, nvidia-smi pstates sampled every 250 ms; best-of-three process medians are used for fits because of per-process power-state bimodality

probe.label: e54bc8d + light grid control + crossing loop disabled (probe, not committed); 2026-10-25
probe.patch: CrossedLights (common/scene.slang) returns zero before its loop; not committed. Images differ from the renderer by construction (MIS-weighted emission found by BSDF sampling is dropped); only timing is used.
